name: Glycogen Storage Disease Due to Glycogen Branching Enzyme Deficiency, Childhood Combined Hepatic and Myopathic Form
aliases: Glycogen Storage Disease Type IV, Childhood Form
Andersen Disease, Childhood Combined Hepatic and Myopathic Variant

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Glycogen Storage Disease Type IV

criteria.description: Demonstration of deficient glycogen branching enzyme activity in liver or muscle tissue
Presence of combined hepatic dysfunction and progressive myopathy in childhood
Liver or muscle biopsy showing abnormal glycogen with fewer branch points and amylopectin-like inclusions
Identification of pathogenic variants in the GBE1 gene
Elevated serum transaminases and creatine kinase levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Deficient glycogen branching enzyme activity plus clinical presentation of combined hepatic and myopathic symptoms in childhood, supported by histopathological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory if enzyme assay and clinical features are definitive.

searchTerms: liver enlargement and dysfunction over time

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive skeletal myopathy with muscle weakness
searchTerms: gradual muscle weakness from skeletal muscle disease

pathognomonic.symptomName: Accumulation of abnormal glycogen (amylopectin-like) in liver and muscle tissues
searchTerms: abnormal glycogen deposits in liver and muscle
storage of abnormal sugar polymers in tissues

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive and growth retardation
searchTerms: failure to gain weight and grow
growth delay and failure to thrive

common.symptomName: Elevated serum transaminases indicating liver injury
searchTerms: high liver enzymes indicating liver damage

common.symptomName: Elevated serum creatine kinase reflecting muscle damage
searchTerms: high creatine kinase showing muscle damage
increased serum CK indicating muscle injury

common.symptomName: Hypoglycemia episodes due to impaired glycogen metabolism
searchTerms: low blood sugar due to glycogen metabolism problems
episodes of low glucose from glycogen issues
scarring of liver progressing to cirrhosis
heart muscle disease with rhythm problems
fluid buildup in abdomen from liver failure
abdominal swelling due to liver failure

rare.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency secondary to muscle weakness
searchTerms: respiratory failure due to muscle weakness

laboratory: Reduced glycogen branching enzyme activity in liver or muscle biopsy
imaging: Ultrasound showing hepatomegaly and liver texture abnormalities
MRI of muscle showing increased signal intensity consistent with myopathy
Echocardiogram revealing cardiomyopathy or conduction defects
other: Histopathology demonstrating amylopectin-like glycogen deposits with fewer branch points
Electron microscopy showing abnormal glycogen structure

distinguishingFeatures: Deficiency of glycogen debranching enzyme instead of branching enzyme
Predominantly hepatic involvement with less severe myopathy
Severe cardiomyopathy and respiratory failure in infancy
Lysosomal glycogen accumulation rather than cytoplasmic

redFlags: Rapidly progressive liver failure in early childhood
Severe muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
